plan.overview:
This one-day itinerary captures the duality of Tokyo, blending historical spirituality with futuristic urban energy. You will begin in the historic heart of Asakusa to witness the cultural weight of Senso-ji temple before traversing the city to the bustling, neon-soaked districts of Shibuya and Harajuku. This path provides a balanced pace, allowing time for quiet contemplation, vibrant shopping, and world-class culinary experiences.

The journey focuses on iconic landmarks, ensuring you see the soul of the city without feeling overly rushed. By leveraging the efficient Tokyo Metro system, you will move seamlessly between neighborhoods, finishing the night with a panoramic view of the skyline and an authentic Izakaya dining experience.
plan.weatherSummary: Tokyo weather varies significantly by season. Spring (March-May) is mild and pleasant; Autumn (Sept-Nov) is crisp and clear. Summers are hot and humid, while winters are chilly and dry. Comfortable walking shoes are a priority year-round as you will be on your feet most of the day.

currencyAndCostEstimate.breakdown: Daily food ~$70, local transit ~$15, attractions ~$35, miscellaneous ~$30

transportationGuide.overview: Tokyo features the world's most reliable rail network. Navigating by train is faster and more cost-effective than taxis.
transportationGuide.recommendedPasses: Suica or Pasmo cards (loaded on iPhone Wallet) are essential for seamless tap-and-go travel on all lines.
transportationGuide.metroBusTips: Download Google Maps for precise real-time train platform numbers and exit navigation.
transportationGuide.airportTransfer: Use the Keisei Skyliner from Narita or the Tokyo Monorail from Haneda for the fastest city center access.
transportationGuide.rideSharing: Uber works in Tokyo but essentially dispatches local licensed taxis. Go or S.RIDE are popular local alternatives.

packingAndPrepTips: Pack portable power banks as navigation apps drain batteries quickly.
Carry a small bag for trash; public bins are rare in Tokyo.
Learn basic Japanese phrases like 'Arigato' (thank you) and 'Sumimasen' (excuse me).
Ensure your credit card supports contactless 'Tap to Pay' for transit gates.
